cita: Galster et al. (2026). A Dataset of Agentic AI Coding Tool Configurations.
problema: No curated large-scale dataset existed that systematically captures HOW developers actually configure agentic AI coding tools (Context Files/Skills/Subagents/Commands/Rules/Settings/Hooks/MCP) across real-world open-source repositories, blocking empirical research on context-engineering and human-AI collaboration patterns.
mecanismo: Not a memory mechanism itself -- this is a measurement/dataset paper: from 40,585 actively-maintained GitHub repos, 36,710 are GPT-5.2-classified as engineered-software projects; of those, 4,738 repos across 5 tools (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Gemini) and 8 configuration-mechanism types are catalogued with full raw file content and per-commit AI-co-authorship metadata (Sec.3, Table 1).
evaluacion: No mechanism performance is evaluated; the paper validates its OWN construction pipeline instead -- an improved LLM classification step reduces 'unsure' (unclassifiable) repositories by 93% versus the authors' own prior study, and reports descriptive statistics across tools/mechanisms/languages (Sec.3-4).
numeros_clave: 15,591 configuration artifacts across 4,738 repos (8 mechanisms x 5 tools); 18,167 raw configuration files with full content; 148,519 AI-co-authored commits (Table 1, Sec.3); 93% reduction in unresolved/unsure project classifications vs prior work (Sec.4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Large-scale field evidence (15,591 artifacts, 4,738 repos, Table 1) that the industry has already converged on version-controlled Markdown/JSON files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style) as agent memory -- confirms MF's Tier-1-docs-as-truth bet is aligned with observed practice, not a speculative design choice.

148,519 AI-co-authored commits give per-commit git-native provenance for these config artifacts (Sec.3-4.3), but the paper does not measure staleness/drift of the artifacts themselves, only their existence and authorship.

notes: Sec.3/Table 1 (8 mechanisms x 5 tools catalogue); Sec.4.2 (93% unsure-classification reduction); Sec.4.3 (AI-co-authorship commit metadata).

cita: Ong et al. (2025). Towards Lifelong Dialogue Agents via Timeline-based Memory Management.
problema: Updating or deleting old memories to keep dialogue memory 'clean' actually destroys important context (e.g. an old but still-relevant persona trait like 'afraid of ships') and degrades response generation, while plain top-k retrieval over a growing memory span misses relevant-but-low-textual-overlap memories.
mecanismo: THEANINE builds a directed memory graph where vertices are (event, time) memories and edges encode temporal + LLM-assigned cause-effect relations (Cause/Reason/Want, Eq.1-8, Sec.2.1), linked at the end of each session (a checkpoint trigger) without ever deleting a memory; retrieval is two-phase (Sec.2.2): top-k by embedding similarity, then extraction of full 'timelines' (the linear path from the graph's oldest connected node) which an LLM refines against the current conversation before response generation.
evaluacion: Automatic metrics (Bleu-4/Rouge-L/Mauve/BertScore, Table 1) plus an ablation (Table 2) isolating relation-aware-linking vs timeline-completeness vs timeline-refinement; plus TeaFarm, a novel counterfactual-driven evaluation (200 questions, Table 4) that avoids G-Eval/human-judge unreliability by tricking the agent with false premises it must correctly reject using its memory.
numeros_clave: Finding 1 (Table 1): methods WITHOUT memory-update/deletion generally score higher than those with update -- direct negative evidence against the common practice of pruning/updating memory; TeaFarm (Table 4, 200 counterfactual questions): THEANINE shows higher success rate than baselines, especially on Conversation Chronicles.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Finding 1 (Table 1) is a direct empirical result that update/delete-based memory hygiene HURTS response quality vs never deleting + linking via a graph -- refutes any MF assumption that 'clean up stale memory' is unconditionally good; the tradeoff needs a graph/linking substrate, not just a delete policy.

Instead of overwriting stale facts, THEANINE preserves the FULL evolution of a fact as a linked timeline (Sec.2.1) -- an alternative staleness-management pattern (preserve+link vs delete) MF could weigh against CareCallmem's opposite conclusion (W4385573343).

notes: Table 1/Finding 1 (no-update beats update); Table 2 (ablation); Table 4 (TeaFarm, 200 counterfactual questions).

cita: Pan et al. (2026). Prometheus: Towards Long-Horizon Codebase Navigation for Repository-Level Problem Solving.
problema: Coding agents navigating large repositories operate as stateless functions across reasoning steps: structure-aware graph retrieval captures spatial topology but not temporal history, so agents repeatedly re-traverse and re-query the same code regions, wasting tokens and fragmenting reasoning across long-horizon issue-resolution tasks.
mecanismo: Prometheus builds a unified knowledge graph of the repo (files/classes/functions + dependency edges) and layers a context engine with working memory: each exploration step writes a ternary record (essential-info/extra-requirement/purpose) linked to reusable context-units (code snippet + metadata), retrieved via 3-vector embeddings + ANN IVFFlat + weighted rerank (Sec.2.2.2); the same graph+memory is shared across 4 specialized agents (issue-classification, bug-reproduction, patch-generation, patch-verification) in a sequential multi-agent pipeline (Fig.2).
evaluacion: Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-PolyBench Verified with GPT-5 as backbone; an ablation (with vs without working memory, 50 SWE-bench issues, Sec.4.3.1/Fig.7) isolates the memory contribution, and a fine-grained retrieval-quality analysis (Table 4) compares hit-rate against human-annotated gold context at file/symbol granularity vs Agentless/OpenHands/SWE-agent.
numeros_clave: Ablation (Fig.7/Sec.4.3.1): with memory 70% resolution / $200.79 cost vs without memory 56% / $367.73 (50 issues) -> -45.4% inference cost, +25% resolution rate; SOTA 74.4% SWE-bench-Verified and 33.8% SWE-PolyBench-Verified (Tables 2-3); retrieval hit-rate 0.915 (file) / 0.850 (symbol), Table 4.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The -45.4% inference-cost / +25% resolution ablation (Fig.7) is direct measured evidence that a persistent working-memory layer pays for itself in token economy, confirming MF's context-economy priority.
Table 4's file/symbol hit-rate against human gold context is exactly the 'measured retrieval' MF wants (ADR-019) rather than assumed retrieval quality.
Sharing one knowledge-graph+working-memory instance across 4 specialized agents (Fig.2) is a concrete single-source-of-context-per-repo seam MF could mirror across its own agents.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Agentic Memory Enhanced Recursive Reasoning for Root Cause Localization in Microservices.
problema: LLM-based root-cause localization in microservices reasons shallowly per-alert (symptom-centric, ReAct/CoT) and re-runs full multi-agent reasoning independently for every alert, causing redundant computation and high latency across the hundreds-to-thousands of alerts in a typical incident window.
mecanismo: AMER-RCL's Recursive Reasoning (RCL) engine performs multi-agent recursive reasoning per alert to progressively refine ranked root-cause candidates; each alert is converted to a causal graph (fingerprint + Graph2Vec embedding + reasoning transcript, Eq.2-3, Sec.4.1.1-4.1.2), and Agentic Memory reuses prior reasoning trajectories for structurally/embedding-similar alerts via a similarity-threshold policy that lets the agent skip, partially reuse, or start from scratch (Eq.4-5, Sec.4.1.2).
evaluacion: Evaluated on AIOPS 2022, Train-Ticket, and FAMOS-Mall against LLM-based (mABC, RCAgent, CoT) and non-LLM baselines, measuring both localization accuracy (MRR) and inference latency/speedup; an ablation (Table 4, Sec.5.5) isolates the contribution of Agentic Memory reuse after IR+CR+FR stages.
numeros_clave: Ablation Table 4 (Sec.5.5): +2.61pp average MRR from Agentic Memory (e.g. 71.13%->73.89% subset A, 72.41%->74.92% subset Z); +14-34pp MRR and 3.5x-31x inference speedup vs baselines (Tables 1-2, Sec.5.1-5.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: 3.5x-31x speedup from reusing prior causal-graph reasoning (Tables 1-2) is strong measured evidence that write-once/reuse-many beats re-deriving reasoning per event, aligned with MF's negative-knowledge/re-derivation stance.
The skip/partial/from-scratch reuse decision is driven by a measured similarity threshold (Eq.4-5), not blind caching -- matches MF's measured-retrieval requirement.

cita: Dong et al. (2025). STARK: Strategic Team of Agents for Refining Kernels.
problema: LLM agents optimizing GPU kernels hit a planning-implementation gap (correct high-level plans fail to translate into valid CUDA) and myopic/redundant exploration (best-of-K wastes attempts, iterative refinement gets stuck in local optima) because prior agents are monolithic and refine linearly from only the immediately preceding attempt.
mecanismo: STARK keeps a persistent search-tree memory T where each node is a kernel candidate plus its runtime/correctness/compiler-diagnostic observations (Sec.4.2), written after every attempt (event-driven write); role-specific dynamic context windows (plan/code/debug agents) are built from the tree's parent/child/sibling relations plus a global top-r leaderboard (Sec.4.4), so the same tree memory is shared across the 3 specialized agents; the plan-agent issues 'grounded instructions' (explicit code-span anchors) that travel as a structured plan to the code-agent, and a strategic epsilon-greedy search policy (root-throttling, dead-branch pruning) balances exploring new strategies vs exploiting known-good branches.
evaluacion: Evaluated on KernelBench (Levels 1-3); an ablation (Table 3) isolates the Search-Agent (tree-memory + strategic search, no multi-agent) against a plain Sampling baseline, and Tables 1-2 compare full STARK against Reflexion and Sampling baselines on success rate and runtime speedup.
numeros_clave: STARK reaches 100% success rate with up to 16x speedup vs Reflexion and 10.7x vs Sampling (Fig.1, Tables 1-2); ablation Table 3 shows Search-Agent alone (memory+search, no multi-agent) already beats Sampling (no memory).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Grounded instructions (explicit code-span anchors) that travel structurally from the plan-agent to the code-agent, recorded as tree nodes (Sec.4.2/4.4), is a concrete plan-state-as-first-class-memory pattern MF could adopt for a handoff=CONTRATO style contract.

One shared tree memory across 3 role-specialized agents (plan/code/debug, Sec.4.4) with role-specific views built from the SAME underlying structure (not 3 separate memories) confirms MF's single-source-per-fact seam design.
Table 3's Search-Agent-alone-beats-Sampling ablation isolates that memory+search (not multi-agent collaboration) is the measured source of most of the gain.

notes: Sec.4.2/4.4 (tree memory + dynamic context windows); Table 3 (ablation); Tables 1-2/Fig.1 (benchmark).

cita: Guo et al. (2025). RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents.
problema: Automated red-teaming agents against code agents restart from scratch on every new attack task, wasting the accumulated knowledge of which jailbreak-tool combinations actually worked before, yielding lower attack success rates and slower convergence than an agent that could learn from its own prior successes.
mecanismo: RedCodeAgent's memory ONLY logs SUCCESSFUL attacks (selective write, Sec.3.2 'Memory Logging'): risk_scenario, risk_description, the full trajectory of tool-calls, the evaluation outcome, and a final self-reflection. Retrieval (Algorithm 1) embeds risk_scenario+risk_description (cosine similarity) MINUS a penalty for trajectory length, so it surfaces the top-K memories that are BOTH similar AND efficient, guiding which red-teaming tool/tool-combination to try next on a new query.
evaluacion: Evaluated on RedCode-Exec, RedCode-Gen, and RMCbench across multiple target code agents (including real assistants Cursor and Codeium); an ablation (Table 5, Appendix D.4) compares a Shuffle condition with vs without the memory module (Shuffle-No-Mem).
numeros_clave: Table 5 ablation (Appendix D.4): memory module improves Attack Success Rate +9.02pp (OCI: 70.25 vs 61.23) and +9.76pp (RA: 77.78 vs 68.02) over the no-memory Shuffle baseline.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Selective admission -- writing ONLY successful trajectories, never failures (Sec.3.2 'Memory Logging') -- is a concrete discretionary-write-trigger pattern (write on verified-outcome, not on every step) relevant to MF's own G-M1 anchor.

Table 5's measured +9-10pp ASR gain from reusing successful past trajectories (vs re-deriving from scratch every time) is direct evidence for negative-knowledge/reuse-over-re-derivation paying off, even outside the memory-safety domain itself (this paper is memory-FOR-attack, not memory-safety, per its own note in Sec.3.2).

notes: Sec.3.2 (selective admission of successful-only trajectories); Table 5/Appendix D.4 (ablation).
